parameter-read.meaning: Reading the formal value within its method; this does not establish which invocation supplied it.

local-read.meaning: Reaching-definition propagation between reads of the same local or receiver. Branch/path feasibility is not established.

assignment.meaning: Assignment, temporary binding, constructor field-formal storage, or an indexed/member write represented by assignment.

parameter-binding.meaning: Actual argument to formal parameter. The saved call context, argument index and resolved callee were checked.

receiver-binding.meaning: Receiver argument zero to the target method receiver. The saved argument index and resolved callee were checked; allocation identity is not proved.

parameter-output.meaning: Read/formal to METHOD_PARAMETER_OUT under shared output-parameter analysis. This is not evidence of a runtime write to immutable arguments.

caller-output.meaning: Output formal to an actual in a calling context. Re-entry and unrelated-caller detours are conservative; not an execution trace.

field-projection.meaning: Receiver/aggregate to a field projection. Whole-object dependence does not prove field-sensitive aliasing or independence.

element-projection.meaning: Collection/string to indexed element projection. Exact indices, multiplicity and heap identity are not established.

alias.meaning: Aggregate/element or local alias propagation without an explicit copied-value assignment in the displayed path. Conservative, not a runtime mutation claim.

operator-value.meaning: Explicit scalar/string/operator result dependency. Boolean predicates, sizes and positions are values but are not necessarily copied element contents.

collection-value.meaning: An element contributes to a constructed collection or its update; exact slots and overwrite precision remain separate obligations.

return-value.meaning: Displayed value to the method return expression; no claim about feasibility of all preceding transitions.

method-return.meaning: Return expression to the method return node.

call-return.meaning: Method return to its call result. The recorded call has the returning method among its resolved callees.

block-result.meaning: Value of a generated expression block, including saved allocation and interpolation results.

capture.meaning: Lexically captured local read in the recorded closure. Capturing a value does not prove callback invocation.

callback-parameter.meaning: External receiver/input to a callback formal through shared unresolved-call expansion. Invocation timing, index-versus-element mapping and lifecycle are not established.

callback-result.meaning: Callback method return to METHOD_REF. The engine abstracts callable identity and its possible result; this is not runtime invocation proof.

callback-effect.meaning: METHOD_REF result abstraction to an external-call receiver/result under stock or explicitly selected summary semantics. Callback side effects and delivery remain outside the path proof.

external-return.meaning: External call/getter/constructor result dependency under the selected semantics. Bodies are outside this graph; selected library contracts must be reviewed separately.

external-write.meaning: Cross-argument or argument/receiver effect at one external call. Saved call identities and positions identify the effect; stock all-argument propagation is conservative. Optional modeled writes apply only within their documented contract.

Saber 0.26.0: actual base64 codec, content/null/type/identity and independent alias mutation. Sass controls retained; no complete app, platform, network, scheduler, quota or encryption execution claim.
Reduced mapped name/index and independent callback-value controls; not full LocalSend applyCounter execution.
Reduced lexical captures and isolated invocations; not external worker scheduling or encryption execution.

representation: Node/call IDs and context/path indices are project-local. transitions[i] classifies elements[i] to elements[i+1]. All retained demand sets in this review are empty. Equivalent stock/modeled paths are shared; full path flags and selected caller contexts are preserved.
reviewMethod: Each selected displayed route was read against its pinned source expectation. Formal argument positions, resolved return targets and available selected frames were checked. Argument-output return evidence already in a caller frame has a separate category. This is a mechanism/approximation review, not branch feasibility, general scheduling or heap qualification.
limitations: Only these twenty-two LocalSend/Saber query families and their returned bounded paths are reviewed; other corpus alternatives and larger searches remain pending.

An endpoint identity is recorded separately from independent forwarding; conservative argument outputs, aggregate projections and external effects do not prove mutation, allocation identity, callback delivery or branch feasibility.
Negative observations retain their same-budget positive controls and explicit query limitations; no absence proof follows from an unfinished search.
